{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABdN-PNA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhGvWUA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 142, "title": "Parallelize browser rendering with an additional Worker without blocking guest emulation and audio", "body": "## Background / current architecture

Issue #136 (completed) moved the Rust/Wasm `Machine` into a dedicated [emulation Worker](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/emulator-worker.js), with [AudioWorklet](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/audio-worklet.js) consuming guest-generated PCM and [the main thread](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/web/app.js) handling Canvas/UI.

**Remaining contention:** one emulation Worker still executes guest CPU instructions, advances emulated devices and guest-clocked audio synthesis, rasterizes the framebuffer through `core.frame()`, copies the complete 640×400 RGBA output, and sends it to the main thread. `app.js` displays this with `putImageData`. Those operations cannot execute concurrently within this single Worker. Heavy frame conversion can delay guest execution and PCM production, while a busy main thread can also affect presentation.

A separate Worker is **not automatically faster**: transferring state, copying 1 MiB frames, synchronizing VRAM/palette changes, and starting more Workers all have costs. We need to isolate useful independent work, preserve guest correctness, and demonstrate improvement on real browser workloads.

## Goal

**Introduce additional dedicated Web Worker(s) for independently executable work—prioritizing video/frame preparation and presentation—so that expensive rendering does not block the CPU/device/audio producer Worker.** Keep browser UI responsive and AudioWorklet glitch-free; improve real throughput and scene-transition responsiveness without changing emulated machine timing.

Evaluate, rather than assume, any benefit from additional audio/DSP or other processing Workers. Do not split the authoritative guest CPU, mutable bus/VRAM, device registers, or virtual clock across concurrent owners unless synchronization and observable ordering can be proven correct.

## Tasks

- [ ] **Measure baseline and identify parallelizable costs** on production release-Wasm in a real Chromium browser (and another supported engine where practical): CPU/guest-slice time, `core.frame()` rasterization, RGBA copy, messages, `putImageData`, main-thread responsiveness, frame latency/drop rate, scene-transition wall time, emulated time per wall second, audio underflow/overflow and PCM queue occupancy. Test representative VM and Ap workloads, including graphics-intensive scene transitions with BGM.
- [ ] **Design explicit ownership boundaries.** Keep a single authoritative emulation Worker controlling `Machine`, CPU, mutable RAM/VRAM, IRQ ordering, IDE/FDD, FM/PCM synthesis and guest clock. Design an independently schedulable render Worker with immutable, timestamped, internally consistent VRAM/text/graphics/palette/EGC/PEGC state snapshots (or another demonstrably safe representation); it must never read mutable state while the CPU writes it. Document snapshot granularity, cost, required data, and backpressure.
- [ ] **Implement an additional video/render Worker** that offloads material frame preparation/rasterization from the emulation Worker. Investigate whether `OffscreenCanvas`/worker-side `ImageData` or transferred frame snapshots work best; select the measured approach. Preserve full VM/Ap display correctness (text/Kanji, graphics, color palettes, GRCG/EGC/PEGC, page switching, blink and refresh timing). Avoid merely moving `putImageData` into another Worker while `core.frame()` remains a bottleneck unless measurements support that choice.
- [ ] **Avoid unbounded copies and queues.** Use bounded transferable buffers and recycling, shared-memory techniques only where justified and compatible with GitHub Pages/static hosting (no mandatory cross-origin isolation), and latest-frame coalescing. Document when a frame is discarded and how a renderer gets an initial/full state after drops. If dirty regions/incremental rendering are used, verify invalidation for palette, mode, glyph, page and register changes.
- [ ] **Preserve A/V and control ordering.** Stamp outputs with guest-time/frame generation; ensure resets, profile switches, pause/resume, media operations and Worker crashes invalidate stale frames. Avoid misordered or partially updated frames and ensure the render Worker never delays PCM refill. AudioWorklet remains the real-time PCM sink, not a place to run emulation or heavy jobs.
- [ ] **Evaluate additional Worker candidates** (e.g., host-only audio sample post-processing, compression/asset preparation, or disk import/export transformations) **only with demonstrated independent work and measured benefit**. Do not parallelize intrinsically ordered guest I/O or change sample timing/pitch to mask CPU overload.
- [ ] **Keep safe fallbacks and deployment compatibility.** Handle browsers without the chosen rendering-worker feature, Worker startup failure and context loss. Preserve static GitHub Pages hosting at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, strict asset/CSP/license audits, sound gesture requirements, media handling, input and existing diagnostics.
- [ ] **Add instrumentation and regression tests** for message/snapshot integrity, out-of-order/stale generations, rapid mode changes, frame coalescing, buffer recycling, bounded memory, Worker fault/recovery and browser integration (release Wasm, real playback).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The default browser path actually uses at least one **additional Web Worker for meaningful rendering or other proven independent work**, not only a new file/idle Worker; heavy image processing no longer serially monopolizes the emulation Worker.
- [ ] Before/after browser measurements with reproducible fixtures, workload descriptions and hardware/browser context demonstrate the effect on emulation throughput, scene-transition latency, render time, UI responsiveness, memory/copy overhead, and audio underflow/overflow. Publish regressions too; do not claim success based only on a higher Worker count.
- [ ] No observable change to deterministic guest CPU/bus/I/O/IRQ sequence, guest-clock timing, sound pitch/tempo, disk integrity, or VM/Ap graphics. Native unit tests and browser/Wasm tests pass.
- [ ] Frames remain coherent under CPU VRAM/palette writes, dropped frames, resets and rapid profile changes; queues/memory are bounded and the fallback path remains functional.
- [ ] Where an extra Worker is not a net win, document the evidence and retain a simpler path rather than forcing further fragmentation.

## Related

- #136 — initial main-thread -> single emulation Worker + AudioWorklet separation (completed; **this issue is the next optimization stage**).
- #138 — guest music/audio fidelity and browser playback validation.
- #140 — hardware-grounded instruction timing; this issue must not change guest cycle semantics to manufacture speedups.

This issue is about **host parallelism and performance**, not running independent unsynchronized emulators or making the virtual PC run faster than its configured hardware.", "url": "https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/142", "created_at": "2026-11-07T05:54:21Z", "state": "OPEN", "repository": "takahirox/pc98-rust", "labels": ["task"], "priority": null, "status": "In Progress", "is_archived": false}, "context": {}, "resources": {}, "allocation": {}, "instruction": null, "run_id": "a7e049f00bc04aa98ac9286d0d22fb2c"}
